lines: אֵי־זֶה שֶׁבַח אָשִׁיר וְאֶתֵּן לְךָ מִשֶּׁלִּי

review: The hymn is the manna-song: 1:1–3 is Ps 36:10 (מְקוֹר חַיִּים) with Jas 1:17, 2:1–4 is John 6:35 (אָנֹכִי לֶחֶם הַחַיִּים) with Ps 23:2 and John 4:14, 3:1–4 is Ps 23:1–4 with Prov 18:10, 4:1–4 is Rom 8:34 with Phil 4:19, and 5:1–4 is Ps 116:12 (מָה־אָשִׁיב לַיהוָה) with Rom 11:33.

Stanza 1 prints three lines, the last two identical; the payload keeps all three with the duplicate verbatim, because the print doubles the 'Fount of graces' line and the doubling is how the refrain settles. Its lines are also shorter than the stanza lines (the print's refrain is a separate 8.8 couplet against the 12.8.12.8 stanzas), so the metre comparison flags them and they are deliberately left short rather than padded.

2:1 הַמָּן הַמַּשְׂבִּיעַ — the Arabic الْمَنُّ الَّذِي يُشْبِعُ is 'the manna that satisfies'; the Hebrew keeps מָן untranslated, as Exod 16:15 does (הוּא הַלֶּחֶם), since the stanza is about the wilderness gift and not about bread in general.

3:1 הָרֹעֶה אֶת־כָּל־הֲוָיָתִי — the Arabic الَّذِي يَرْعَى وُجُودِي says 'tends my existence'; הֲוָיָה is post-biblical for 'being', used because the line has to name the whole of one's life and the psalm's צֹאן would narrow it to the flock.
